subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy layer, make cron inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep cron limited to per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This is a permanent public config and security boundary choice, and the safer precedence relative to existing policy layers and stored cron jobs is not something automation should decide.

options.title: Add explicit cron policy layer
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` as a named cron-only policy layer, document precedence against per-job `toolsAllow`, and cover fresh and upgrade behavior in tests.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy for cron
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as subagent-like for tool restrictions, reducing new config surface but coupling cron behavior to spawned-agent semantics.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Leave `payload.toolsAllow` and delivery safeguards as the supported path, avoiding new config but leaving no operator-wide cron deny knob.

recommendation.title: Add explicit cron policy layer
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` as a named cron-only policy layer, document precedence against per-job `toolsAllow`, and cover fresh and upgrade behavior in tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to the current subagent policy lines and already reviewed this exact issue as requiring maintainer follow-up.
